science_disclosure_paragraphs: Sea of Okhotsk, LME_052. The selected model describes the whole sea. Regional workbook
Catch source
Sea Around Us, 1950–2019 reconstructed catch. Reference: 2019 landings; all 151 exact reporting labels, including zero catch. Original catch
Selected article

Chaikina (2004), A trophic mass-balance model of the Sea of Okhotsk for the 1980s period. BSc thesis, UBC, 49 pages. Original thesis unavailable. A related 2020 chapter documents the earlier model. Thesis listing | Related chapter

Radchenko (2015), Characterization of the Sea of Okhotsk Ecosystem Based on Ecosystem Modelling. A 48-group contemporary model is retained as an alternative; full reconstruction is unreviewed. Alternative article
Selected model

52_1_Sea_of_Okhotsk_NE_(1980). NE means newly constructed detailed Ecopath. It is a whole-sea 1980s annual-average model with 29 source groups and computational import 30. Reported area: 1,590,000 km². Accepted model

The same source also compares a simplified nine-group SD 1980s model derived from the Shuntov–Dulepova food web. NE and SD are model structures, not northeastern and southern subregions. Simplified model

Article — Retained as the broadest located whole-sea model despite incomplete original documentation.Model — The detailed NE structure supplies finer biological resolution; existing numerical caveats remain.

All supplied native Table 1 B/PB/QB/EE values agree with accepted inputs. The accepted diet contains 74 normalized cells from eight printed columns totaling 0.998–1.001. Native catch fields and pollock cutoff are absent; export zeros, detritus B=1 and existing defaults/balance remain accepted assumptions. Source fidelity

Temporal fit

Static 1980s coefficients and fixed biomass proportions transfer across 1950–2019 whole-LME landings, catch and discards. Reference 2019 is roughly three decades later. Seasonal source averaging does not reconstruct annual catch composition or ecosystem change.

Weights and assumptions: native group catches are unavailable. Canonical export=0 is not an observed stage fraction. Complete source biomass supplies every multi-group vector at Medium allocation confidence. Pollock supplies 48.9157% of 2019 landings and is allocated 53.874619% adult/nonjuvenile and 46.125381% juvenile, with equal catchability assumed and no recovered cutoff. Fixed 1980s proportions apply across all years and catch bases. Each rule table partitions the same simple-chain PPR. Complete candidate vectors

Unresolved: Cyprinidae, because unobserved freshwater family composition supplies no defensible local marine home. It retains 177.054315 t landings and 1,241.263560 t C classic PPR in the denominator. Very low: 46 labels, 11.0196% landings and 4.1872% classic PPR. These include broad bony/invertebrate unions and unrepresented cartilage, pelagic and grazing-fish analogues. Source Salmon is mostly zooplanktivorous, limiting tuna/shark transfer.
